videos.title: What a neuron actually does
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 1 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain how a neuron receives, adds up and sends signals.

videos.title: The action potential, step by step
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 2 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Draw the action potential and say which ion does what at each phase. Watch first: What a neuron actually does.

videos.title: Synapses: how neurons talk
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 3 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Describe chemical synaptic transmission and excitation versus inhibition. Watch first: The action potential, step by step.

videos.title: Dopamine is not the pleasure chemical
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 4 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain dopamine as a learning signal (reward prediction error). Watch first: Synapses: how neurons talk.

videos.title: How the brain learns: plasticity
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 5 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain Hebbian learning, LTP and why practice changes the brain. Watch first: Synapses: how neurons talk.

videos.title: Measuring the brain: EEG, MEG and fMRI
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 6 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Say what each method measures, and its time and space resolution. Watch first: The action potential, step by step.

videos.title: Brain networks and rhythms
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 7 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain oscillations (alpha, gamma...) and functional networks without myths. Watch first: Measuring the brain: EEG, MEG and fMRI.

videos.title: Real neurons vs artificial neural networks
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 8 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Compare what deep learning borrowed from the brain and what it did not. Watch first: How the brain learns: plasticity.

videos.title: GPT for brain signals: EEG foundation models
videos.seriesInfo: Neuroscience from Zero, part 9 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain how a model pretrained on lots of EEG is reused for new tasks, and its limits. Watch first: Real neurons vs artificial neural networks.

videos.title: What is a signal? From sound to EEG
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 1 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Describe signals in time, and the idea of amplitude, frequency and phase.

videos.title: Sampling and the Nyquist rule
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 2 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Choose a sampling rate and explain aliasing with an example. Watch first: What is a signal? From sound to EEG.

videos.title: The Fourier transform without fear
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 3 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Compute and read a spectrum in Python and say what the FFT is doing. Watch first: Sampling and the Nyquist rule.

videos.title: Filters: keeping what you want
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 4 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Design and apply low-, high- and band-pass filters, and see their side effects. Watch first: The Fourier transform without fear.

videos.title: Noise, artifacts and cleaning real recordings
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 5 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Spot and remove line noise and artifacts in a real EEG recording. Watch first: Filters: keeping what you want.

videos.title: Feedback and control: how a thermostat thinks
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 6 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain feedback loops and PID control with a simulation. Watch first: What is a signal? From sound to EEG.

videos.title: Project: build an EEG band-power analyser in Python
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 7 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Go from a raw open dataset to band-power plots, with code in the repo. Watch first: Noise, artifacts and cleaning real recordings.

videos.title: Brain-computer interfaces: how they actually work
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 8 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain the BCI loop - record, decode, feed back - and what limits speed and accuracy. Watch first: Noise, artifacts and cleaning real recordings.

videos.title: Decoding typed sentences from brain signals (Brain2Qwerty)
videos.seriesInfo: Signals and Systems, Explained, part 9 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Walk through a non-invasive brain-to-text study: setup, model, results and what it cannot do. Watch first: Brain-computer interfaces: how they actually work.

videos.title: Set up Python for data analysis
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 1 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Install Python, Jupyter and pandas, and run a first notebook.

videos.title: pandas: load, explore, clean
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 2 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Load a real CSV, find missing and wrong values, and fix them reproducibly. Watch first: Set up Python for data analysis.

videos.title: Plots that tell the truth
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 3 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Pick the right chart and avoid misleading axes and averages. Watch first: pandas: load, explore, clean.

videos.title: Statistics you actually need
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 4 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Use mean, median, variance and distributions correctly, with real data. Watch first: Plots that tell the truth.

videos.title: p-values, done correctly
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 5 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Say what a p-value is and is not, and run a test without p-hacking. Watch first: Statistics you actually need.

videos.title: Correlation, regression and confounders
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 6 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Fit a regression and explain why correlation is not causation, with an example. Watch first: p-values, done correctly.

videos.title: Machine learning with scikit-learn, honestly
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 7 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Train, validate and test a model and catch data leakage. Watch first: Correlation, regression and confounders.

videos.title: Project: analyse an open dataset end to end
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 8 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Question, clean, analyse, model and present, with the notebook in the repo. Watch first: Machine learning with scikit-learn, honestly.

videos.title: Machine learning on brain scans with nilearn
videos.seriesInfo: Data Analysis from Zero (Python), part 9 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Decode a condition from fMRI data with nilearn and validate it without leakage. Watch first: Machine learning with scikit-learn, honestly.

videos.title: Market data in Python: prices, candles, returns
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 1 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Load price data and compute simple and log returns correctly. Watch first: pandas: load, explore, clean.

videos.title: Risk first: volatility and drawdown
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 2 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Measure volatility and maximum drawdown and explain why they matter more than returns. Watch first: Market data in Python: prices, candles, returns.

videos.title: Build a backtester from scratch
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 3 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Write a simple event-by-event backtester and test it on a toy strategy. Watch first: Risk first: volatility and drawdown.

videos.title: Costs and slippage: why most backtests lie
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 4 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Add fees and slippage and show how much they change the result. Watch first: Build a backtester from scratch.

videos.title: Overfitting, look-ahead and survivorship bias
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 5 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Recognise the three biases in real backtests and test against them. Watch first: Costs and slippage: why most backtests lie.

videos.title: Walk-forward testing and out-of-sample data
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 6 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Split data properly and validate a strategy walk-forward. Watch first: Overfitting, look-ahead and survivorship bias.

videos.title: Position sizing and risk management
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 7 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Size positions by risk and explain why sizing matters more than signals. Watch first: Walk-forward testing and out-of-sample data.

videos.title: Paper trading, regulation and staying honest
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 8 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Paper trade safely and know what SEBI rules mean for advice and tips. Watch first: Position sizing and risk management.

videos.title: Can you detect a bubble? The LPPLS model, tested honestly
videos.seriesInfo: Algo Trading with Python - Education Only, part 9 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Fit LPPLS to a past bubble and show why its predictive power is debated. Watch first: Walk-forward testing and out-of-sample data. Education only. Test on past data and show the failures as clearly as the hits.

videos.title: What psychosis is, and what it is not
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 1 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Describe psychosis accurately, without stigma, and separate it from movie myths. Mental-health rules in writing-style.md apply to this whole series.

videos.title: What is computational psychiatry?
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 2 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain why maths and models are used to study mental illness. Watch first: What psychosis is, and what it is not.

videos.title: The predictive brain
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 3 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain predictive coding: the brain as a prediction machine that learns from errors. Watch first: Dopamine is not the pleasure chemical.

videos.title: When predictions go wrong: predictive coding and psychosis
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 4 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain how altered prediction and precision could lead to hallucinations and delusions. Watch first: The predictive brain.

videos.title: Dopamine and aberrant salience
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 5 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain the aberrant salience hypothesis and what evidence supports and limits it. Watch first: When predictions go wrong: predictive coding and psychosis.

videos.title: Modelling belief updating: reinforcement learning and Bayesian models
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 6 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Fit a simple learning model to choice data and read its parameters. Watch first: Dopamine and aberrant salience.

videos.title: Brain signals in psychosis: EEG and mismatch negativity
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 7 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain mismatch negativity and why it is studied as a marker in psychosis. Watch first: Noise, artifacts and cleaning real recordings.

videos.title: Inside my PhD: a computational psychosis study, start to finish
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 8 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Walk through a real study's question, data, model and limits. Watch first: Modelling belief updating: reinforcement learning and Bayesian models. Only what is published or cleared to share. TODO: confirm what can be shown.

videos.title: How decisions are made: drift diffusion models
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 9 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Fit a hierarchical drift diffusion model to choice and reaction-time data and read it. Watch first: Modelling belief updating: reinforcement learning and Bayesian models.

videos.title: Information flow in the brain: transfer entropy
videos.seriesInfo: The Computational Brain: Psychosis Research Explained, part 10 of 10
videos.notes: You will learn to: Explain transfer entropy and compute it between two signals with JIDT, with its pitfalls. Watch first: How decisions are made: drift diffusion models.

videos.title: How to learn any technical subject properly
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 1 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Use active recall, spaced practice and projects instead of rewatching videos.

videos.title: How to read a research paper
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 2 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Read a paper in three passes and pull out the question, method and limits.

videos.title: Finding papers: Google Scholar, PubMed and arXiv
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 3 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Search the literature systematically and keep track of what you read. Watch first: How to read a research paper.

videos.title: Reproduce a paper: the best first research project
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 4 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Pick a paper with open code and data and reproduce one result. Watch first: Finding papers: Google Scholar, PubMed and arXiv.

videos.title: How to start research as an undergraduate
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 5 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Find a lab or project, write to a professor and apply for summer research programmes.

videos.title: Writing your first paper
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 6 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Structure a paper and know what reviewers look for. Watch first: Reproduce a paper: the best first research project.

videos.title: Failure, rejection and motivation in research
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 7 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Handle failed experiments and rejections with a plan, not panic.

videos.title: PhD life, honestly
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 8 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Give a realistic picture of a PhD: time, money, supervision, and what makes it worth it.

videos.title: Transcribe and search your lectures with WhisperX
videos.seriesInfo: Learn It Right: Research Skills for Students, part 9 of 9
videos.notes: You will learn to: Turn recorded lectures into searchable, timestamped notes on your own computer. Watch first: How to learn any technical subject properly.
